answer: The prover commits to a set inclusion proof over the registry of claimants, and the proof is small because it carries the exclusion of every competing holder, so two identities claiming the same resource would have to produce contradictory proofs. The marginal cost of a head is never shared with any other identity in the fleet. The trellis is the unique resource, the jetty the proof that excludes every other holder, and the river the registry that makes the exclusion checkable; cloning the trellis forces two contradictory jetty proofs, and the river is where the contradiction shows.
